templates.protocol:
OUTPUT FORMAT
Write natural text and registered self-closing Action tags. Use only aliases from the callable Action list below; quote all attribute values. Do not invent Actions, parameters or Channels.
SCHEDULING: CHANNEL, EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS, WAIT
A Channel is an ordering queue, not a device module. Within this task, Actions on the same Channel execute in output order, each waiting for the previous Action to finish. Different Channels may run concurrently; output order alone does not order their completion.
An Action address identifies its domain, module and function. The runtime independently enforces registered serialization and resource constraints across tasks and Channels. Changing a Channel never bypasses these constraints. Different addresses may share constraints; parallel execution is allowed, never guaranteed.
Use each Action on its listed default Channel by emitting its self-closing tag directly. Do not wrap Actions in Channel tags merely to name their default Channels. Actions with different default Channels already have independent queues; for concurrent behavior, emit their tags directly without Channel wrappers or wait groups. Use a Channel scope only when intentionally overriding the listed default for a specific ordering requirement. Each Action uses its listed default Channel unless enclosed in <channel.NAME>...</channel.NAME>, using an available Channel name. This overrides the Channel of enclosed text and Actions. Closing the scope restores the outer scope or each Action's own default. Channel tags neither wait nor stop Actions; no name has special main-channel behavior.
Use <wait>...</wait> for execution dependencies. Before its contents can start, all earlier work in its parent group must finish. Inside the group, normal Channel ordering and execution constraints still apply. Later work in the parent cannot start until the group is closed AND all its Actions and nested groups have finished.
The whole response has an implicit root group. Nested waits apply the same rule within their own parent only; they never wait on themselves, ancestors or unrelated tasks. A group may start received Actions before its closing tag arrives. <wait></wait> is a valid empty synchronization point. Wait does not change Channels.
Patterns (A, B, C and D are placeholders for actual Actions or natural text, not tags to output): <wait>A B</wait><wait>C D</wait> completes the first group before starting the second. <wait>A <wait>B C</wait> D</wait> completes A before B/C, and completes B/C before D. B/C may overlap only on different Channels and compatible execution constraints.
SYNTAX RULES
Channel and wait tags must be paired, properly nested and attribute-free. Never cross closing tags or write <wait/> or a self-closing Channel. Action tags must be self-closing. At most 32 wait groups, 8 combined Channel/wait nesting levels and 120 generated Actions are allowed.
Escape literal < and & in text as < and &; use " for quotes inside double-quoted attributes. Do not output a document root, comments, DOCTYPE, CDATA, paired Action tags, parallel/serial tags or sync attributes.
Wait coordinates only the current task and adds no implicit timeout or rollback. Emitting a tag is a request, not proof that its effect occurred.
AVAILABLE CHANNELS: {{channels}}
Natural-text interpretation is supplied by the calling Agent; text alone implies no execution effect.
ACTIONS BY DEFAULT CHANNEL (use the Action alias as the XML tag):
templates.action: Action {{alias}}: path={{path}}; default Channel={{channel}}; required string parameters={{required}}; optional={{optional}}.
templates.communicationDescription: Directed task communication. Authorized targets: {{targets}}. Allowed kinds: {{kinds}}. request creates a task and must omit taskID; input/progress/result/cancel requires taskID. Content is plain task text, never internal/UI commands. Acceptance is not task completion. progress asks for user input and keeps the task open; do not follow it with result. result completes it. Include artifactID for artifact-specific questions. Examples use placeholders; replace them with the current task identity and actual content.
